correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructible full proof: each edge contributes the symmetric 3-by-3 moment block, giving M=[3D-A,-B;-B^T,3I]; BB^T=D+A and Schur give det M=3^m(4/3)^n det(2D-A). The all-ones centering lemma multiplies by N/K^N and yields the exact pseudo-determinant. Cauchy–Binet proves the forest expansion with roots weighted by degree. Schur for stars and the path continuant prove both exact determinant formulas and exponential rate. Two six-vertex tree determinants and common covariance trace follow by exact finite arithmetic. An independently coded direct point-moment checker passed 187 connected simple graph/tree instances and the recurrence through 13 vertices. Finite checks support but do not substitute for universal algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: The three highly relevant primary papers establish respectively the definition, face/tree normalized volume, and triangulations of graph cosmological polytopes, not the equal-weight vertex covariance pseudodeterminant. Matrix–forest expansions are preexisting and credited; the novel assessed implication is their exact connection with this polytope inertia determinant and the exponentially separated volume-matched tree examples. All relevant comparison searches and inspected sections are enumerated; undetected alternate formulations remain possible.
residual_risks: An equivalent inertia/scatter identity may be published under covariance of graph configuration, signless Laplacian forest polynomial, or cosmological-polytope metric terminology and missed by search.
The 2006 matrix–forest source was checked via its abstract; the underlying forest formula is explicitly credited and independently proved here.
The research claim does not assert any independent validation or guarantee of comprehensive prior-art coverage.

value.rationale: Degree-rooted forests yield a natural all-graph interpretation of vertex inertia and a closed spectral invariant in the canonical Euclidean realization. Polytope volume is identical for all fixed-order trees but the volume of their equal-mass vertex-inertia ellipsoids can differ exponentially; same-degree six-vertex twins even share covariance trace yet differ in this determinant. This explains an actual geometric distinction invisible to lattice volume and low-order degree data rather than a routine recomputation of a tabulated polytope count.
